problem_statement: The State Machine Framework has no way to observe what a state machine does as it runs. A user should be able to register hooks on a state machine context (after setting the initial state) that are notified before each entry, run, and exit action executes (with the state and the action type), after each transition (with the source and destination states), and when an invalid operation is detected (such as a NULL transition target or a transition attempted from an exit action). When the feature is disabled, there should be no runtime overhead and the state machine behaves exactly as before. The tests install such hooks and assert the exact sequence of recorded actions, transitions, and errors across flat, hierarchical, 5-ancestor, and self-transition state machines, including normal flows and termination in entry/run/exit actions.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/lib/smf -s tests/lib/smf/libraries.smf.flat -s libraries.smf.flat -O twister-out --no-clean -W
